title: Unauthorized Location Sharing
description: Child's device transmits live GPS coordinates to backend without explicit consent or appropriate privacy controls

title: Sensitive Information Transmission
description: Personal location data is transmitted to backend system, potentially exposing child's movements and habits

title: Unintended Location Tracking
description: Live GPS data could enable unauthorized tracking of child's movements by third parties or malicious actors

title: Location data stored beyond necessity
description: Location pings are written to the Location History Store without clear justification for retention period or necessity, violating the minimality principle for personal data collection and storage.

title: Location data accessible to unauthorized parties
description: Location History Store may be accessible to unauthorized users or systems, leading to implicit disclosure of location data to third parties or internal stakeholders without proper authorization controls.

title: Location data leakage through metadata
description: Location data stored in the History Store may leak through metadata, timestamps, or derived information that could be used to infer sensitive user behavior patterns.

title: Unintended privacy consequences of location storage
description: Storing location history may have unintended privacy consequences such as enabling profiling, tracking, or correlation with other data sources without user consent.

title: Potential regulatory non-compliance for location storage
description: Storing location data may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding consent, purpose limitation, or data retention requirements for location-based personal data.

title: Location data disclosure to geofencing engine
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) transfers user location pings to Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2). This explicit data disclosure involves sharing personal location data across a process boundary, which may exceed the minimality principle if location data is not strictly required for the geofencing functionality.
assumptions: Location data is considered personal data under applicable privacy regulations.

title: Location data disclosure to third parties
description: Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) may process and potentially disclose location data to external third parties (e.g., analytics services, advertising partners) for zone-based targeting or reporting purposes, which may not be explicitly authorized by users.
assumptions: P2 may have downstream data sharing capabilities not modeled in this flow.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if P2 has downstream data sharing - this is a potential risk that should be verified.

title: Location data linking with other user data
description: Location pings from P1 could be linked with other user data (e.g., account information, purchase history, communication metadata) to create comprehensive user profiles, potentially revealing sensitive information about user habits, social activities, or health status.
assumptions: P1 may have access to or integration with other user data stores.

title: Inference of sensitive user behavior from location data
description: Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) processes location data to determine zone entry/exit, which could be used to infer sensitive information about user activities, health status, social interactions, or daily routines without explicit user consent.
assumptions: Location data patterns can be used to infer sensitive user behaviors.

title: Lack of control over notification data usage
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) may not have control over how the parent external entity (EE1) uses the arrival/departure notification data, potentially leading to unauthorized processing or sharing of location-based information.

title: Unintended use of location notification data
description: The arrival/departure notification data may be used by the parent entity for purposes beyond the intended geofencing/alert function, such as profiling, marketing, or other data aggregation activities.

title: Excessive information disclosure
description: The notification may contain more information than the parent entity (EE1) actually needs for their intended purpose, potentially including unnecessary location details or timing information.

title: Data retention concerns
description: There may be insufficient controls over how long the arrival/departure notification data is retained by the parent entity, potentially leading to excessive data accumulation and increased privacy risk.

title: Inadequate Information About Data Collection
description: Parent may not be adequately informed about what personal data (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) is being collected during account registration and profile creation.
assumptions: Parent may not read or understand privacy notices during registration.

title: Insufficient Consent for Data Collection
description: Parent may not be providing explicit, informed consent for the collection and processing of child's personal data during registration.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may be unclear or not properly implemented.

title: Lack of Parental Control Over Data
description: Parent may not have adequate control over their child's profile data after registration, including ability to review, modify, or delete information.
assumptions: System may not provide clear data management interfaces for parents.

title: Unintended Use of Collected Data
description: Data collected during registration (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) may be used for purposes beyond what was stated to the parent.
assumptions: System may have secondary data uses not disclosed during registration.

title: Unintended Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Personal data (account, child profile, geofence zone) may be disclosed to third parties through unintended data sharing, data breaches, or improper access during storage in DS2. The minimality principle may not be fully applied, potentially collecting more data than strictly required.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure Without Consent
description: Account and child profile data may be explicitly disclosed to third parties (e.g., advertisers, analytics partners) without explicit consent from the family account holder, violating privacy expectations and consent requirements.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure Through Metadata
description: Geofence zone data may be disclosed implicitly through metadata or derived from other disclosed data, potentially revealing location patterns and family member information without explicit disclosure.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Data
description: Stored account, child profile, and geofence zone data in DS2 may be accessed by unauthorized parties due to insufficient access controls, weak authentication, or security vulnerabilities in the storage mechanism.

title: Information Leakage Through Data Breach
description: Personal data stored in DS2 may be leaked through data breaches, system failures, or security incidents, resulting in unintended disclosure of sensitive family account information.

title: Location data accuracy
description: Parent may receive inaccurate or outdated location information about the child, potentially leading to safety concerns or misinformed decisions.
assumptions: Location data is transmitted from the mobile app backend to the parent without real-time verification.

title: Information completeness
description: Parent may not receive complete location history or current location data, potentially missing important safety information.
assumptions: Data filtering or truncation occurs during transmission from the mobile app backend.

title: Location data retention
description: Location data may be retained longer than necessary or without proper deletion mechanisms, increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: Data retention policies are not clearly defined or enforced for location history data.

title: Privacy policy compliance
description: Location data sharing may not comply with applicable privacy regulations or the parent's consent requirements.
assumptions: Data processing activities are not fully documented or aligned with privacy policies.

title: Location History Retrieval
description: Location history data is retrieved from the data store to the mobile app backend, potentially exposing sensitive user movement patterns and location-based behavior that could be used for profiling or tracking.

title: Information Overexposure
description: The location history data retrieved may contain more detailed or comprehensive information than necessary for the stated purpose of serving the parent's map/history view, potentially exceeding user expectations.

title: Data Transfer Risk
description: Location history data is transferred from the data store to the process, creating a potential point where data could be intercepted, logged, or mishandled during the transfer.

title: Unintended Data Usage
description: The retrieved location history data could potentially be used for purposes beyond the stated map/history view functionality, such as targeted advertising or behavioral profiling.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's location to secondary guardian
description: Parent (EE1) shares child's location data with a secondary guardian (grandparent/relative) without explicit consent from the child or appropriate authorization. This disclosure may violate the child's privacy rights and create risks of location tracking beyond intended boundaries.

title: Location data linkability to child's identity
description: The location data shared with the secondary guardian can be linked to the child's identity, enabling tracking of the child's movements and activities. This linkability creates privacy risks as the secondary guardian may infer sensitive information about the child's whereabouts, routines, and social interactions.

title: Location data disclosure at destination
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) receives and processes the child's location data from the parent. This destination element may store or process the data in ways that could lead to unauthorized disclosure to third parties or create persistent records of the child's location history.

title: Unauthorized Location Sharing
description: Live location data is shared with secondary guardian without explicit consent or proper authorization verification

title: Information Disclosure to Unauthorized Parties
description: Child's location information may be disclosed to secondary guardian who lacks proper authorization or has not been properly vetted

title: Unintended Consequences of Location Sharing
description: Sharing live location with secondary guardian may lead to unintended tracking, surveillance, or misuse of child's location data

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Secondary guardian may not comply with data protection regulations regarding handling of child's location data

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of User Analytics
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics shared with external advertising partner may contain personally identifiable information or be used for purposes beyond the intended scope, leading to unauthorized disclosure of user behavior patterns.

title: Unintended Data Usage by Partner
description: Advertising/analytics partner may use the shared analytics data for purposes other than funding the app's free tier, such as building user profiles for targeted advertising or selling data to third parties.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in Data Sharing
description: Sharing user analytics with external third parties may violate privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.) without obtaining proper user consent or providing adequate privacy notices.

title: Inadequate Security Controls at Partner
description: External advertising/analytics partner may have insufficient security measures, increasing risk of data breach or unauthorized access to the shared analytics data.

title: Non-repudiation of SOS message
description: The system may not be able to prove that the child actually sent the check-in/SOS message, as there could be no cryptographic signature or audit trail to attribute the message to the specific user.
assumptions: Assumes the system relies on manual input without authentication or digital signature mechanisms.

title: Confidentiality of location data
description: Location data transmitted in the SOS/check-in message could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially exposing the child's real-time location to attackers.
assumptions: Assumes the communication channel may not be fully encrypted or protected.

title: Integrity of location data
description: The location data sent in the SOS message could be tampered with or corrupted during transmission, potentially leading to incorrect location information being processed by the parent.
assumptions: Assumes the communication channel may not be fully protected against tampering.

title: Accuracy of location data
description: The location data sent in the SOS/check-in message may be inaccurate or incomplete, potentially leading to the parent receiving incorrect location information.
assumptions: Assumes the child may not be aware of or may not be able to provide accurate location information.
